$comment: Hub-owned inputs to scripts/deploy/preflight_sibling_floors.py.
The preflight DERIVES most of its work: module-scope sibling imports come
from an AST scan of this repo, and floors come from pyproject.toml. This
file holds only the parts that cannot be derived, because deriving them was
measured to be impossible rather than merely inconvenient.
extra_import_probes exists because of 2026-08-22. /api/plot/ returned 500 to
every well-formed request (control: malformed requests correctly returned
400 throughout) and the failing import was NOT at module scope -- it was a
function-scope 'import scitex as stx' followed by the lazy attribute touch
'stx.plt.load_style()' in apps/infra/public_app/api_plot_helpers.py:293-295.
An AST scan of module-scope imports cannot see it. Neither can pip: the two
packages that were missing, scitex-sh and scitex-decorators, are declared in
no pyproject in the chain -- not hub's, not scitex's, not scitex-io's -- so
no floor comparison and no dependency resolver could have caught them.
Executing the import in the target is the only thing that reaches them.
Measured that day: 'import scitex' left 29 sibling distributions loaded;
one 'stx.plt.load_style()' pulled six more -- figrecipe, scitex_clew,
scitex_decorators, scitex_io, scitex_sh, scitex_stats. That is why entries
here name submodules and attributes and not just the umbrella: the prod
image where 'import scitex.io' raises ImportError still prints a perfectly
happy 'import scitex OK 2.29.3', which is exactly what the existing boot
check (deployment/docker/common/lib/scitex.src:10) asks -- green on the
broken artifact, and running after the recreate where it can only report an
outage rather than prevent one.
ignore_import_roots keeps the derived set honest. hub's OWN wheel provides
scitex_hub and scitex_cloud, and importlib.metadata maps scitex_container to
BOTH scitex-hub and scitex-container, so treating them as siblings would ask
the target about hub's own source tree.

extra_import_probes.why: The umbrella itself. Green even on a broken artifact -- kept as the control that proves the probe reaches a working import, so an all-fatal result is distinguishable from a probe that cannot import anything at all.

2026-08-22 outage, exact shape. scitex/io/_load.py:33 does 'from scitex.decorators import preserve_doc'; with scitex-decorators absent the umbrella's _aggregator raises ImportError and /api/plot/ 500s. Measured absent from scitex-hub-prod-django:latest on 2026-08-22 and present only in the running container's writable layer, so this probe is the one that fails on the artifact the next recreate will run.

The attribute the outage actually touched. 'import scitex.plt' alone can pass while the lazy resolution of an attribute raises, because scitex/__init__.py defers to _LazyModule and only __getattr__ reaches the real distribution.

scitex/__init__.py:153 maps scitex.sh -> scitex_sh via _LazyModule. Until 2026-09-05 neither hub's pyproject nor scitex's declared scitex-sh, so no floor check could see it; hub now declares scitex-sh>=0.2.0 (pyproject). The probe stays: a floor proves a version was resolved, this proves the lazy import actually reaches a module in the image.

scitex/__init__.py:97 maps scitex.decorators -> scitex_decorators, the other half of the 2026-08-22 pair. Declared by hub since 2026-09-05 (scitex-decorators>=0.1.12); the probe stays for the same reason as scitex.sh — it is what scitex.io's own loader imports first.
Pulled by the same load_style() touch; undeclared by hub.
Already smoke-tested at image build time (Dockerfile.prod), but only there -- the build smoke test cannot see the boot overlay that replaces five siblings at every container start.
